a novel alkane degrading consortium was established, and that the key players in the consortium were Smithella and Methanocalculus.

A methanogenic alkene-degrading (a C9 to C 12n-alkane mixture) culture was established from production water of an oil reservoir and assessed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel methanogenic alkanothrophic consortium that can initiate n-alkanes degradation by fumarate-addition mechanism.
a novel alkane degrader, which can activate alkanes by fumarate and is capable of syntrophic growth with methanogens.
the biodegradation of n-alkanes under methanogenic condition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the alkane-degrading culture established in the present study was a consortium of syntrophic alkane degraders and methanogens.
the enrichment culture was able to degrade C9 to C 12n-alkane by fumarate-addition mechanism, which is initiated by Smithella and completed by methanogens.
alkane activation is not restricted to a specific mechanism and that the alkane-degrading community is highly flexible and adaptable to changing environments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Smithella initiates the degradation of C9 to 12n-alkane by the fumarate addition pathway, which is subsequently followed by the hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis of the alkylsuccinate products by the hydrogenotroph Methanocalculus.
the alkane degradation in the enrichment cultures is a syntrophic process between alkane-degrading Smithella and hydrogenotrophic and acetoclastic methanogens.
the alkane-degrading culture was enriched by Smithella and the methanogens were enriched by the syntrophic association between alkane-degrading Smithella and methanogens.
The main takeaway from our work is that
alkane degradation by fumarate activation is not restricted to the anaerobic oxidation of methane process, but can also occur in alkane-degrading methanogenic communities.
the enrichment cultures of alkane-degrading methanogenic consortium can be used as inocula for the biodegradation of alkane in low-temperature oil fields.

the alkane-amending enrichment culture established from production water of low-temperature oil fields can be used as a model system to study the biodegradation of alkanes under methanogenic condition.
